items.title: SQL injection in the users search
items.plain_explanation: Whatever someone types in the ?name= box is pasted straight into a database query. An attacker can type SQL instead of a name and read or delete your whole users table.

items.title: Hard-coded API secret
items.plain_explanation: Your API secret key is written directly in config.ts. Anyone who can see your code, including on GitHub, can use it as if they were you.

items.title: Hard-coded payments token
items.plain_explanation: A payments API token is stored in the source code. Someone who copies it could make payment requests on your account.

items.title: Cross-site scripting on /hello
items.plain_explanation: The /hello page shows the name from the URL as HTML. A link with a script in it would run that script in your visitor's browser.

items.title: lodash 4.17.15 has a known vulnerability
items.plain_explanation: Your app uses lodash 4.17.15, which has a published security bug (prototype pollution, CVE-2020-8203). Updating fixes it.

items.title: CORS allows every website
items.plain_explanation: Your API tells browsers that any website may call it. A malicious site could make requests to your API from your users' browsers.

items.title: No security headers
items.plain_explanation: Your server doesn't send the standard security headers that tell browsers to block common attacks such as clickjacking.

items.title: Server listens on a fixed port
items.plain_explanation: The port number is fixed in code. That's fine for development; most hosts expect it to come from the PORT environment variable.

details.title: SQL injection in the users search
details.what: The /api/users route builds its SQL by inserting the name parameter into the query text.
details.why_it_matters: Anyone on the internet can change what the query does, for example dump every user's email and password hash.
details.how_to_fix: Pass the value as a parameter instead: pool.query("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = ?", [name]). The database then treats it as data, never as SQL.
details.snippet_redacted: const [rows] = await pool.query(`SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '${name}'`);

details.title: Hard-coded API secret
details.what: config.ts contains an API secret as a plain string.
details.why_it_matters: Secrets in code end up in git history, screenshots and shared repos. Leaked keys are found and abused within minutes.
details.how_to_fix: Move it to an environment variable (process.env.API_SECRET_KEY), put the value in a .env file that is listed in .gitignore, and rotate the old key.

details.title: Hard-coded payments token
details.what: config.ts contains a payments API token as a plain string.
details.why_it_matters: Payment credentials are a direct path to money. They must never be in code.
details.how_to_fix: Load it from process.env.PAYMENTS_API_TOKEN, keep the value in .env (gitignored), and rotate this token with your provider.

details.title: Cross-site scripting on /hello
details.what: The name query parameter is inserted into an HTML response without escaping.
details.why_it_matters: An attacker can send your users a link that steals their session or acts on their behalf.
details.how_to_fix: Escape the value before putting it into HTML, or send it as text: res.type('text/plain'). A template engine with auto-escaping also fixes it.

details.title: lodash 4.17.15 has a known vulnerability
details.what: A dependency version in package-lock.json has a known security advisory.
details.why_it_matters: Attackers scan for apps with known-vulnerable libraries because the exploit is already public.
details.how_to_fix: Run npm install lodash@latest (4.17.21 or newer), then commit the updated package-lock.json.

details.title: CORS allows every website
details.why_it_matters: Other sites can read your API's responses through a visitor's browser.
details.how_to_fix: List only your own front-end address: cors({ origin: ["https://yourapp.com"] }).

details.title: No security headers
details.what: The Express app doesn't use helmet or set headers like Content-Security-Policy and X-Frame-Options.
details.why_it_matters: These headers are a cheap extra layer that stops whole classes of browser attacks.
details.how_to_fix: npm install helmet, then add app.use(helmet()) right after creating the app.

details.title: Server listens on a fixed port
details.what: app.listen uses config.port, which is hard-coded to 3000.
details.why_it_matters: Not a vulnerability. It only affects how easily you can deploy.
